svg.title: Along any logarithmic path where the finitely many radii have rates, induction on this tree proves the corresponding affordable-expression rate. The leaf uses the full field bound, multiplica- tion uses separated products, carrying uses coarsening, and the two projection steps use the full tested remainder and output estimates with the displayed gains. All use the same hierarchy and reader, and the remaining component is kept as its signed difference. To obtain a uniform bound in the radii, normalize their logarithms as in the nested expansion proof and pass to a compact refining limit. The product surcharge Q R−ε supplies a strict positive rate margin against any j proposed violation. Hence an expression of price p satisfies
